ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence (EDD) for all applicants, directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and senior management against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit domestic sanctions and watchlist, the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions, and commercially available PEP databases. Any individual classified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) must have source of wealth and source of funds independently verified by a senior compliance officer and approved by the board. Continuous transaction monitoring and periodic re-screening at least every 90 days is required for the duration of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour) – Companies Online Services; Samoa International Companies Registry via a licensed registered agent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in the basic Latin script and Samoan alphabet; if a name is desired in a foreign language or script, an English/Samoan transliteration must be provided and cleared by the Registrar. The name must contain a limited-liability suffix such as Limited, Corporation, Incorporated, or S.A. Names that are misleading, identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name will be rejected. Samoan-language names are permitted provided they do not contravene the Ministry's language and public-order guidelines.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days by filing an application with the Companies Registrar before the initial reservation expires. Upon any name rejection, the applicant may file a written objection with the Companies Registrar within 14 days; the Registrar must issue a written determination within 21 days. If the objection is unsuccessful, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 days. A final remedy may be sought through judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa no later than six months after the ministerial decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is generally not permissible for the licensed Electronic Money Institution. The International Company may maintain its registered office at the registered agent's address in Samoa, but the licensed EMI business requires a physical operating presence with local personnel, compliance records, and IT infrastructure accessible to the Central Bank of Samoa and the Financial Intelligence Unit. A purely virtual or non-physical registered office will not satisfy the licensing and commercial substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – 80% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 18 months of licensing, with mandatory on-site examinations expected at least annually thereafter.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; ss 6-16 (Incorporation), s 8 (Memorandum and Articles), s 10 (Registered Office), s 12 (Share Capital), s 52 (Directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (M&A) filed together with Form 1 – Application for Incorporation of an International Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account is required. The authorized capital and paid-up capital are as stated in the statement of capital filed with the Registrar; a Samoa International Company may allot shares for no par value and need not deposit any paid-up capital in escrow before commencement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company subscribes to the initial issued capital set out in the statement of capital filed with the Registrar of International Companies, and such shares are allotted to the founding subscriber accordingly. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at the address of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and that office remains open during normal business hours for statutory purposes. RESOLVED that the persons named in the incorporation filings be appointed first directors and officers, and the directors and a corporate officer are authorised to execute financial account documents, and to submit the electronic money institution licence application and all regulatory filings to the Central Bank of Samoa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent supervised by the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed registered agent and provide the proposed company name and at least three alternatives. The agent conducts a name-search in the SIFA international company register and certifies that the desired name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing Samoa-registered entity. Upon clearance, the agent issues the incorporation kit and fee schedule.
required_dossiers: Company name reservation request with three alternative names
Passport copies of each director and ultimate beneficial owner
Proof of residential address for each principal
Letter of engagement with the licensed registered agent
Brief statement of proposed electronic money and digital wallet business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for being identical or confusingly similar, the proposed name must be amended and a fresh name reservation request submitted with alternative names; no monetary penalty is imposed for an initial rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public / Licensed Registered Agent (pre-filing verification)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English by the subscriber, incorporating the statement of capital, share allotments, director consents, and the registered agent's acceptance of the registered office. All copies of identification and corporate due-diligence documents must be notarized or apostilled as required by SIFA practice.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed by the subscriber)
Statement of capital and share allotment record
Consents to act from each director and the corporate secretary
Registered office acceptance signed by the licensed agent
Notarized or apostilled identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is defective or signatures irregular, the document must be re-executed and corrected under the agent's supervision and refiled within five working days; SIFA may reject only for substantive non-compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) – Companies Registration Desk / e-Registry Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Form 1 – Application for Incorporation of an International Company together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, statement of capital, registered office details, and director consents. Pay the official government filing fee by telegraphic transfer into the SIFA-designated account and retain the bank receipt. Thereafter monitor the portal for the certificate.
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Application for Incorporation of an International Company
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Statement of authorized and allotted capital
Consents to act of each director and company secretary
Registered agent certificate appointing the registered office in Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a requisition, file a response or amended documents within 14 days of the requisition notice. If the application is rejected, correct the specified defects and resubmit the application with a nominal resubmission fee; the agent may appeal to SIFA if the rejection is made in error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Post-Incorporation Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / SIFA and Central Bank of Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to adopt the pro-forma first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, and appointment of officers. Record the minutes and maintain them in the statutory corporate register. Upon issue of the Certificate of Incorporation, apply for the Certificate of Good Standing from SIFA, register any tax-exemption or foreign investment filings with the Ministry of Revenue, and submit a pre-application notification to the Central Bank of Samoa for the electronic money institution licence.
required_dossiers: Adopted pro-forma first board resolution
Minutes of the first board meeting
Certificate of Incorporation
Directors' and officers' appointment declarations
Share register and statement of capital
Central Bank of Samoa pre-licence notification letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation is withheld due to overdue fees, pay the outstanding government fee and request release within 24 hours. If the Central Bank notification is rejected or questioned, amend the business description to make 'electronic money issuance and digital wallet management' the sole or primary activity and resubmit the notification through the licensed agent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Central Bank of Samoa – Licensing and Supervision Department

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) – Environmental Assessment and Management Unit
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Registration (low environmental risk); no full Environmental Impact Assessment required for an office-only electronic money institution with no industrial manufacturing operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge is expected. If backup diesel generators are installed, the facility must comply with MNRE waste management regulations: fuel tanks must be bunded, all wastewater and contaminated discharge retained for licensed disposal, generator exhaust emissions must meet WHO ambient air quality guidelines, and electronic waste, including worn servers and SIM hardware, must be collected by government-approved e-waste recyclers with chain-of-custody documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) confirming exit signage, fire extinguishers, smoke detection, and emergency lighting; structural load clearance from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI) for the premises, including the data-server / vault area; and an occupational health clearance from the Ministry of Health for indoor air quality, electrical safety, and safe workplace facilities. The EMI must also maintain a business continuity and physical security plan covering 24-hour access control, CCTV, and anti-fraud protection of the e-money operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue (MOR), Government of Samoa, acting through the Commissioner of Revenue; official public portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws; electronic filing and taxpayer self-service portal: Integrated Revenue Administration System (IRAS) at https://services.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate an International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 2017 with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation, the constitutional documents, and the IC registration number; SIFA is the licensed registrar and also supervises the registered agent and the annual licence renewal obligation. Step 2 — Apply to the Ministry of Revenue for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) through IRAS using Form TIN-01, submitting the following: certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation, the IC's constitutional documents, the registered agent's letter of engagement identifying the directors and the ultimate beneficial owner, a certified passport copy of each director and shareholder, and evidence of the licensed EMI activity (Central Bank of Samoa in-principle licence or authorisation letter under the Financial Institutions Act). Step 3 — If the IC will make any taxable supplies in Samoa or if annual worldwide taxable turnover in respect of supplies consumed in Samoa exceeds WS$100,000, file the VAGST registration application (Form VAGST-01) through IRAS simultaneously with the TIN application; in the absence of any Samoa nexus the IC need not register for VAGST. Step 4 — The Ministry of Revenue issues a unique nine-digit TIN, and the VAGST registration number where applicable, within statutory processing time; because the IC's international business income is statutorily exempt, no corporate income tax registration or annual income tax return is due, but the IC must file an annual economic substance declaration and pay the SIFA annual renewal fee, and must keep the registered agent informed of changes in directors, shareholders, and the principal place of business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — International Company (IC) established under the International Companies Act 2017. The default statutory classification is an exempt offshore vehicle fully outside the income tax net of Samoa in respect of international business activities: profits, gains, and foreign-source income derived by the IC are exempt from Samoa income tax, there is no capital gains tax, no withholding tax on dividends or interest paid to non-residents, and no estate, inheritance, or gift duty on offshore assets. The exemption is territorial in scope: any income falling within the domestic-source rules of the Income Tax Act 2015 (for example, profits from business carried on in Samoa or from services rendered to Samoa residents) would be assessable at the prevailing corporate rate, subject to the IC's powers under its constitutional documents. Additionally, the IC is not a resident person for exchange control purposes and benefits from the Exempt zone regime of the International Companies Act 2017, which also grants the IC freedom from statutory audit and public filing of financial statements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no check-the-box or partnership-filing election available in Samoa; entity classification is fixed by statute. The only elections relevant to this IC are: (i) the voluntary election to maintain international company status and thereby remain outside the Income Tax Act 2015 by satisfying the ongoing requirements of the International Companies Act 2017, including the annual SIFA licence fee and economic substance declaration; and (ii) the election to voluntarily register for VAGST where annual taxable supplies are below the WS$100,000 mandatory threshold, subject to the Commissioner's discretionary acceptance. Samoa has not enacted BEPS Action 2 hybrid-mismatch rules, and no domestic hybrid-mismatch election exists; artificial hybrid arrangements are instead recharacterized under the general anti-avoidance rule in the Tax Administration Act 2015 and the transfer-pricing rules of the Income Tax Act 2015, which would apply only if domestic-source income were present.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WS$100,000 (annual value of taxable supplies) — the compulsory VAGST registration threshold under the VAGST Act 1994; a non-resident IC supplied wholly offshore digital financial services to non-residents has no VAGST nexus and is not obliged to register, but if the IC imports the services or incurs local input-taxed costs while remaining unregistered it cannot recover input VAT, and any incidental Samoa taxable turnover above the threshold triggers mandatory registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate is currently in force in Samoa. The Ministry of Revenue operates the IRAS platform for electronic VAT return filing, e-payments, and taxpayer correspondence; all registered persons must issue and retain prescribed VAGST tax invoices containing the supplier's TIN, the customer's TIN, date, description, and amount of tax charged, and must retain records for five years. Samoa is advancing its revenue-administration digitalisation roadmap under IMF technical assistance, but no mandatory SAF-T, continuous transaction control, or clearance-by-stamp regime has been enacted.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods qualifies for the 0% VAGST rate when the goods are exported from Samoa within 28 days of supply (or such longer period as the Commissioner allows) and the exporter retains acceptable proof of export; a supply of services is zero-rated when the services are supplied to a non-resident customer who is outside Samoa at the time the services are rendered, which covers the offshore digital financial services of this licensed EMI, including virtual IBAN issuance, digital wallet reserve management, cross-border payment processing, and correspondent clearing fees. Where the IC is registered for VAGST, these zero-rated export supplies remain taxable supplies for the purpose of input tax credit recovery, so the IC is entitled to refunds of VAGST charged on its local business inputs (for example, Samoan legal, audit, and registered agent fees); where the IC remains unregistered, no VAGST recovery is available and the cost of local inputs is economically borne by the IC.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs export declaration (CusDec) lodged electronically through the ASYCUDA World system, with the customs officer's release endorsement
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment and exportation within the statutory time limit
Commercial invoice describing the exported goods and stating the zero-rated consideration

Underlying cross-border service contract, SEPA or correspondent-clearing settlement statement, and the customer's non-residence supporting evidence (certificate of incorporation, registered office certificate, or passport copy) for digital financial services treated as an export supply
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign currency account credit advice issued by a licensed Samoa commercial bank evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in Samoa
VAGST input tax invoices issued by local suppliers and the payment gateway or wallet issuer's settlement records supporting the input credit claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry of Revenue and the Samoa Customs Service apply enhanced audit scrutiny to zero-rated export supplies by licensed financial institutions. A false zero-rating claim, fabricated export documentation, or a knowingly incorrect tax invoice is prosecuted under the VAGST Act 1994 and the Tax Administration Act 2015: the Commissioner may issue a retrospective clawback assessment disallowing the zero rate, recover all underpaid VAGST, and deny or recover input tax refunds, with the assessment period extended to up to six years in ordinary cases and up to ten years where fraud or wilful neglect is established. Civil shortfall penalties are graduated up to 100 percent of the tax evaded depending on culpability, statutory late-payment interest continues to accrue until full settlement, and criminal conviction for tax evasion or fraudulent invoices can attract substantial monetary fines and a term of imprisonment for directors, officers, and any accomplice, including the licensed registered agent, who participates in the falsification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Apia, Samoa; the CBS is the national monetary authority and exchange-control administrator under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1978. The Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) administers the International Companies Act 2017 and acts as the registry and licensing body for international financial services entities, including the international company that will hold the electronic-money/banking special licence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tālā (WST) is a non-deliverable currency subject to current and capital account exchange controls. Current account payments in respect of bona fide trade in goods or services may be converted and remitted through an authorized dealer once documentary evidence is presented and the transaction is reported to CBS. Capital account inflows such as equity injections, shareholder loans, virtual IBAN reserve funding, and crypto-to-fiat conversion-related treasury balances generally require prior CBS approval or confirmation through an authorized commercial bank. Profit remittance is available to non-resident shareholders only after annual audited financial statements prove distributable reserves and the company has settled any domestic tax or withholding obligation; the remitting bank must complete the CBS capital-account approval application and obtain an exchange control release before USD conversion and transfer. Practical hurdles for an EMI include slower remittance cycles, additional documentary layers for beneficiary ownership behind trusts, CBS statistical reporting of all non-resident transfers, and the lack of a deep offshore WST market. There is no market-driven WST convertibility outside Samoa; offshore lenders or hedge counterparties typically require WST/USD NDF or bank letters of credit.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBS exchange-control notices, all export proceeds must be collected through an authorized dealer in Samoa within 90 days from the date of export or service performance. Unless an exemption is granted, all foreign exchange export receipts must be converted into WST at the prevailing bank rate within that timeline and the conversion must be reported to CBS. For a licensed electronic-money international company, the practical application is limited to (i) actual Samoan export goods or services invoiced by the Samoa entity and (ii) inward remittances characterized as service fees or settlement consideration for e-money issuance. The company must maintain the underlying commercial agreements, invoices, freight/customs evidence, and bank credit advisements for five years. If the EMI is structured as a pure offshore international company deriving only foreign-source financial intermediation income, CBS may permit foreign-currency retention with a specific surrender exemption; however, the default regulatory position is full repatriation and conversion of export-value proceeds into WST unless otherwise approved in writing.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Samoa does not have a dedicated EU/UK-style electronic-money institution licence. An offshore digital wallet and virtual-IBAN business may be carried on only through a Samoa-licensed international financial services provider or an international banking special licence approved by SIFA and CBS. Foreign-regulated EMI companies cannot provide services directly into Samoa without establishing a local licensed entity or a licensed financial services provider. The business plan is viable as a non-resident-facing treasury entity if the Samoa international company holds (i) a SIFA international financial services/electronic-money licence or international banking licence, (ii) segregated reserve accounts with a Samoan authorized dealer, and (iii) a physical principal office in Samoa for AML/CFT governance. Digital-only onboarding of end-customers from the EMI platform must be governed by the Samoan bank’s AML/CFT policy; no foreign EMI passporting is recognized. SEPA Credit and central-bank clearing are not direct membership products of a Samoa international company; they require a European partner bank or an SEPA-participating agent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory. At least one director and one authorized signatory must attend an in-person KYC/AML interview at the bank’s premises in Apia or at a recognized overseas office of the banking group before any Samoan account is opened. Remote opening is not available under the Central Bank of Samoa’s core AML/CFT requirements except for a second signatory added after the initial account opening. The bank will require original passports, proof of residential address, certificate of incorporation issued by SIFA, memorandum and articles, beneficial-ownership registry extract, certificate of good standing, board resolution appointing signatories, professional references, a foreign bank reference letter for each UBO, and a business plan describing the EMI’s payment flows, client jurisdictions, and expected monthly transaction volumes. For directors that cannot travel to Samoa, an alternative is to appoint a Samoan resident professional director through a licensed corporate services provider; that Samoan director must appear and the non-resident economic owners must still complete a video interview plus notarized identity documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore International Company with bearer-share history or an opaque Pacific trust layer: high-money-laundering-risk entity classification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current SIFA certificate of good standing; certified registry extracts identifying all issued shares; beneficial ownership declaration naming each natural person; complete trust deed and trustee resolution if a trust is shareholder; explanatory statement of the commercial rationale for the Samoa structure; previous banking relationship references; AML/CFT compliance certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual IBAN and digital wallet pass-through risk: customer payments arriving at the Samoan bank without clear originator or beneficiary details
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ownership and licence documentation for the EMI; compliant customer onboarding files; transaction monitoring rules; source-of-funds programmes; real-time sanctions screening evidence; audit opinion on internal controls; a robust AML/CFT policy that is materially aligned with FATF and CBS requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk source of funds: cryptocurrency trading proceeds, electronic money storage, unregulated regional money-transfer operators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements showing the exact fiat trail; wallet addresses and transaction hashes with paid-chain analysis from a reputable blockchain analytics vendor; exchange licence details and KYC/AML policy of the crypto counterparty; tax statements or tax-residence certificates for UBOs; sworn source-of-wealth declaration; rejection dossier for any untraceable or mixed-funds source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Chinese-speaking traditional family wealth with surname transfers: enhanced cross-border financial and influence risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Biographical résumés, valid passports, bank references, credit reports, corporate records, real-estate or business ownership corroboration, notarized family wealth-structure chart, and independent legal opinion from a recognized Chinese-speaking law firm explaining the legitimacy of the trust or cross-border shareholding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP connected directly or indirectly through a family or charitable foundation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial PEP-screening report; legal opinion confirming PEP status and degree of influence; source-of-wealth statement corroborated by tax and employment records; transaction monitoring increased-risk treatment notice; approval by the Samoan bank MLRO and, if required, CBS notification before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No physical substance in Samoa: bank perceives shell entity and risks regulatory censure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for serviced offices in Apia; photographs and board-meeting minutes; staff employment contracts and social insurance records; Samoan director’s declaration of actual governance; SIFA annual return; current bank statements; accounting records prepared by a Samoan licensed accountant to demonstrate activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder-loan funds must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 to the Samoan bank’s receiving branch. The remitter must state the exact corporate name, SIFA registration number, and the purpose as ‘Shareholder Capital Injection / Financing of Licensed Electronic Money Institution — ISIC 6619’ (BPM6 code for direct investment equity). Before execution the Samoa bank must accept the CBS Exchange Control capital-account application, verify that the incoming funds are not encumbered by anti-money-laundering red flags, and obtain copies of the board resolution, share subscription agreement, or facility agreement. Funds are initially credited to a Capital Escrow Account and cannot be released to the operating account until the bank completes the secondary source-of-funds check and the exchange-control approval (or deemed approval) has been recorded. For non-WST currencies the bank will convert only the amount actually required for Samoan operating expenses; the balance may remain in an approved foreign-currency account if CBS has issued a retention permission. The EMI must also file a CBS inward-foreign-direct-investment report through the receiving bank, giving the transaction reference, economic sector, UBO country, and expected use of funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements and EMI treasury payments are executed on SWIFT MT103, MT202 COV, and documentary commercial letters of credit using the bank’s SWIFT BIC and corresponding banking network. A Samoa-licensed International Company has no direct central-bank clearing or SEPA membership; SEPA Credit transfers are possible only through a European partner bank or a SEPA-participating account. For every outward remittance the company must provide supporting invoices, contracts, licences, and FX confirmations, and the bank will apply sanctions screening, OFAC/UN/EU/BIS list screening, and CBS reporting. Commercial LC settlements (MT700 issued or MT707 amendment) require presentation of transport documents, commercial invoices, packing lists, inspection certificates, and insurance documents; the proceeds are paid into the Samoan operating account and retain the same anti-money-laundering audit trail as cash transactions. Since the EMI is treated as a non-bank financial institution, the bank may require outbound disbursements to be pre-notified within CBS’s daily or weekly FX reporting windows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/WST forward contracts with an authorized dealer in Samoa, restricted to hedging an identified current or capital account exposure, with physical WST settlement at maturity.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/WST) with a licensed Samoan bank, subject to CBS approval and used exclusively for cash-flow hedging of foreign-currency liabilities or assets.
Structured forwards with an authorized dealer for translation of tier-2 subordinated debt, provided the underlying debt is approved by CBS and does not consist of offshore WST retail deposits.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) against the WST executed through a CBS-approved international bank and settled in USD; Samoa is a non-fully-convertible currency, so the NDF must have an underlying aggregate treasury exposure and match the EMI’s trade and net-settlement schedule.
FX spot purchases through authorized dealer banks for same-day settlement of e-money redemption obligations, with no speculative open-currency position held overnight.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return in the prescribed form under the Samoa International Companies Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days from each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs monthly penalty surcharges; persistent default for three consecutive months may trigger administrative strike-off after 60 days' notice by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government License Fee (International Company Renewal Fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on the anniversary of incorporation; due no later than 60 days after that date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment attracts penalty interest at 10% per month or part month; after three months in arrears the Registrar may commence strike-off proceedings under the International Companies Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Annual Continuation Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed registered agent in Samoa (maintained as statutory corporate record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On each anniversary of incorporation or within 30 days after any change of agent or office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a licensed registered agent and registered office in Samoa may lead to administrative non-compliance notices and eventual strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies and Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (where applicable under AML/CFT regulations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation or within 30 days after any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted UBO filing constitutes an offence subject to monetary penalties and possible imprisonment of responsible officers; continued violation may lead to deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Electronic Money Institution Annual Regulatory Return and Licensed Activity Submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the financial year, and at such intervals as prescribed in the e-money license conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission or material misstatement may result in license suspension, revocation, or a monetary supervisory penalty imposed by the Central Bank of Samoa.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for all licensed electronic money institutions regulated by the Central Bank of Samoa, irrespective of size or revenue. Unlicensed international companies may be exempt from audit only if shareholder consent is recorded in accordance with the International Companies Act and no regulatory condition requires audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), as adopted by Samoa Financial Reporting Standards, for licensed financial institutions. General international companies use IFRS or Samoa GAAP equivalently for their internal accounts preparation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a beneficial ownership register and confirm the accuracy of UBO information at least annually. For any shareholding transfer or change of significant control, the UBO register must be updated within 14 days and the annual confirmation to the Registrar must reflect that change; licensed e-money institutions must also provide UBO confirmation to the Central Bank of Samoa.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% effective rate for a Samoa International Company (wholly exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, and stamp duty under the International Companies Act 1987); 25% headline corporate rate applies solely to domestic taxable companies conducting Samoa-source business outside the exempt-IC perimeter
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Complete statutory tax exemption for international companies: no CIT, no capital gains tax, no stamp duty on instruments, no exchange control on foreign currency accounts, and no tax on dividends, interest, or royalties paid to or received from non-residents. The only recurring fiscal cost is the annual government license fee calculated on the authorised share capital band plus the licensed registered agent fee. The fee substitutes for income taxation and preserves the Tax_Exempt_Zone classification.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return and Declaration for International Companies (ICA Form AR-1) filed through the Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) e-Registry portal; no income tax return is filed for exempt international-company income, and the annual return to the Registrar serves as the sole periodic compliance instrument alongside the annual government fee declaration
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Return for the prior year must be submitted within 30 days of the annual incorporation anniversary; the annual government fee must be remitted by the anniversary date. Any domestic-source taxable activity creating a filing obligation would follow the Income Tax Act 2012 rule requiring the corporate income tax return within 90 days after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, International Company registration number, date of incorporation, and jurisdiction of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact registered legal name; non-resident beneficial owners are identified by full legal name and country of residence; nominee details are disclosed to the Registrar only under the AML/CFT beneficial-ownership declaration protocols

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in Samoa and appointed licensed registered agent (a Samoa-licensed trust company or corporate services provider)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A licensed agent in Apia is mandatory for every International Company; foreign directors and shareholders may hold office without any Samoan residence, but all service-of-process and regulatory correspondence flows through the local agent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory declaration of continued compliance with the International Companies Act 1987, confirmation that no Samoa-source taxable business has been conducted, and confirmation of economic substance reporting obligations under the Economic Substance Regulations 2021
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Signed by a director or by the licensed agent on behalf of the board; an intentionally false declaration constitutes a criminal offence and may expose the non-resident beneficial owner to enforcement action through the agent's regulator

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Register particulars: directors, shareholders, issued and authorised share capital, and beneficial ownership declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Minimum one director and one shareholder; no residency or nationality restrictions; bearer shares are prohibited, and the beneficial-ownership schedule must be maintained at the registered agent's office in Apia

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual government fee computation based on the authorised share capital band and proof of payment remitted through the licensed agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fee payable in Samoan Tala or US Dollars to the Samoa International Financial Services Authority; the licensed agent issues the payment receipt and files the declaration on the non-resident owner's behalf

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fixed penalty plus a daily surcharge per day of continuing default; unpaid annual government fees incur a percentage surcharge and interest; persistent default triggers compulsory strike-off and dissolution of the International Company, forfeiture of the exempt regime, and potential aggregation of liability against the licensed registered agent for negligence

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% withholding tax on dividends paid by an International Company to non-resident shareholders where the exempt-IC income and distribution satisfy the International Companies Act 1987 conditions; the domestic non-resident dividend withholding tax rate is 15%, which applies only where an International Company derives non-exempt Samoa-source income and the distribution is recharacterised as taxable
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa's operational double tax agreement network is limited (New Zealand DTA in force, with further treaty engagement on an as-needed basis). To invoke treaty relief, the beneficial owner must obtain a Samoa certificate of residence issued by the Ministry of Revenue or, for exempt international companies, a SIFSA tax-residency confirmation; the claim is submitted to the paying party, who files the withholding tax reconciliation with supporting treaty forms, and the reduced treaty rate is conditional on the payee being the beneficial owner with no conduit-entity arrangement and on annual economic substance being demonstrated under the 2021 ESR regime
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: 15% on interest and 15% on royalties paid to non-residents on Samoa-source income; no withholding applies to foreign-source income earned by an International Company nor to interest and royalties paid to an exempt International Company by non-resident counterparties; under the New Zealand DTA the source-state withholding on interest and royalties is capped at 10%, subject to certification of residence and arm's-length substance requirements

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is required where annual related-party transactions of an International Company exceed WST 1,000,000 (approximately USD 375,000); a Master File is required where the multinational group's consolidated turnover exceeds WST 25,000,000; the documentation must support the arm's-length outcome of all cross-border dealings with associated enterprises of the electronic-money and digital-wallet reserve business
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Samoa Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) 2021 apply to International Companies conducting relevant activities, including banking, financing, digital payment services, distribution, and headquarters functions. An Electronic Money Institution issuing Virtual IBANs and holding digital-wallet reserves must demonstrate substantial economic presence in Samoa: local board governance, a physical office, adequate qualified employees engaged in core income-generating activity, and an annual ESR report lodged with SIFSA. Passive-income-only shell structures without local substance are treated as non-compliant and exposed to exchange of information and penalty proceedings

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a false annual declaration that no Samoa-source taxable activity exists while the International Company in fact derives non-exempt domestic income, or fraudulently using the exempt-IC regime to conceal a Samoan commercial establishment operating an unlicensed money service
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of up to 150% of the tax understated plus default interest; corporate fines up to WST 250,000 under the Income Tax Act 2012; deregistration of the International Company; reference to international tax transparency blacklists by the OECD or EU where the arrangement is presented as a tax-evasion vehicle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the licensed agent are jointly and severally liable for restitution of the evaded revenue; conviction carries imprisonment up to 7 years, disqualification from acting as a director or trustee in Samoa, and seizure of corporate records to support civil recovery against foreign beneficial owners

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Electronic Money Institution as a pure shell with no physical presence, no local employment, no board meetings in Samoa, no ESR filing, and no substance behind the Virtual IBAN and reserve-management activity while recycling foreign payments through the Samoa entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic Substance Regulations penalties of WST 50,000 for the first breach and WST 100,000 for each continuing breach; mandatory disclosure to the Samoan competent authority for international information exchange; strike-off and liquidation under the International Companies Act 1987; loss of the tax-exempt license for the EMI activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face civil recovery for unpaid government fees and substance deficiencies, travel bans pending regulatory inquiry, and debarment from serving as directors of any Samoa International Company; criminal breach of duty carries imprisonment up to 5 years and personal liability for third-party losses caused by the non-substantive structure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism Violations (Electronic Money Institution)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deploying the Samoa International Company as an unlicensed EMI to issue Virtual IBANs and host digital-wallet reserves without a Samoa AML/CFT license, without customer due diligence and beneficial-ownership verification, or while concealing the identity of high-risk counterparties from the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to WST 1,000,000, revocation of any special financial-services license, and suspension of the International Company's registration under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2017; asset-freezing orders, mandatory segregation and wind-down of customer reserve accounts, and referral to overseas payment-rail regulators for violations of scheme rules of Central_Bank_Clearing or SEPA_Credit corridors
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior officers and directors risk criminal prosecution carrying imprisonment up to 14 years, personal fines up to WST 500,000, confiscation of proceeds, and, given the banking_aml_risk_tier of High_Risk_Special_License, an automatic ban from all financial-sector roles within Samoa and reciprocal debarment from equivalent fintech licensing regimes abroad

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Repatriation Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recharacterising disguised management fees, wages, interest, or royalties as tax-exempt dividend distributions out of non-exempt Samoa-source profits, or using artificial shareholder loans to strip accumulated value without arm's-length interest while claiming the 0% dividend withholding position
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding tax reassessment on the true character of the payment, a grossed-up penalty of up to 50% of the withholding shortfall, and statutory default interest; denial of the New Zealand DTA benefits where residence or beneficial-ownership substance requirements are not met; possible reclassification of the International Company as a taxable domestic company for the offending income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the offending distribution or loan resolution are personally liable for the unrecovered withholding tax and statutory penalties; criminal prosecution for tax evasion carries imprisonment up to 7 years, while civil fraud actions permit recovery directly against personal assets of the directors, including by way of asset tracing through the licensed agent's records
